subject: physics

hotspots.label: Positive Ball
hotspots.description: The + ball carrying the positive charge protons would represent.
hotspots.colorHint: Warm amber sphere on a thin stem.
hotspots.function: Represents the kind of charge that pulls negatives.

hotspots.label: Negative Ball
hotspots.description: The − ball rich in electrons — the mobile carriers.
hotspots.colorHint: Cool blue sphere on its stem.
hotspots.function: Represents the electron-loaded side that can move.

hotspots.label: Force Arrows
hotspots.description: The push/pull markers spanning the gap between the two balls.
hotspots.colorHint: A double arrow that points together or apart.
hotspots.function: Shows attraction or repulsion direction live.

hotspots.label: Discharge Spark Path
hotspots.description: The spark rail that gives the charge a path to balance along.
hotspots.colorHint: A thin blue-amber rail across the bench.
hotspots.function: Provides the route for the crowd of electrons to rebalance.

visualStyleNotes: Warm off-white paper ground, soft vignette. Small laboratory bench with two charge balls on stems, arrows between, and a fine spark rail.
materialNotes: Metallic=0, roughness ~0.5. Balls brightly saturated; sparks thin lines; no emissive bloom.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: positive and negative electric charge attraction/repulsion.

GEOMETRY: a bench (y=0.3) with ball stems at x=-0.7 and +0.7, amber + and blue − spheres of y=0.7; a force arrow between them; a discharge rail (0,0.2,0.3) crossing the bench.

INTERACTION: sign buttons per ball; arrows aim toward (attract) or away (repel); the discharge switch runs a spark along the rail and zeroes the arrows.

NAMED NODES: Bench, BallPos, BallNeg, ForceArrows, SparkRail, SignButtons. 6-8k tris.
